newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London mixed in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London mixed in quiet trade.

text.p: U.S. shares were mixed in thin trading volumes on Monday as many European investors started their Christmas holidays early, dealers here said.
"There has been very little business. A lot of people haven't bothered to come in to work and probably won't be back until the New Year," one market maker said.

"I wouldn't be too surprised to see the Dow drift down a bit today. Futures and bonds are weaker so we could see some profit-taking." The March S&P 500 futures contract traded on the Globex after-hours trading system, was down 1.25 at 756.00 by 1045 GMT.

AT&T was down $1/4 at $39-1/8 after news that Joseph Naccihio, the head of the company's consumer long distance unit, had resigned to take over Quest Communications, a firm that specialises in leasing fiber-optic lines.
IBM eased $1/2 at $154 following an article in the lastest edition of Barron's which claimed the company's profits may have been inflated by the use of "arcane" accounting rules.

Elsewhere, Apple was up $3/8 at $23-7/8, continuing to benefit from news that the computer company's co-founder Steven Jobs, was returning, more than 11 years after he was ousted in a stunning boardroom coup.
